original_question: For Su's 1997 system of supplementary-variable equations for a two dissimilar unit system with three modes and random checks, with state probabilities p0,0,k(x,t), p1,0,0(x,t), p0,1,0(x,t), p1,1,0(x,t), p0,1,1(x,t), p1,0,1(x,t), p0,2,0(x,t), p2,0,0(x,t), p1,1,1(x,t), p1,2,0(x,t), and p2,1,0(x,t); transition rates lambda1,0, lambda2,0, lambda0,1, lambda0,2; check rate alpha(x); and repair rates mu_i,0(x), mu_0,i(x), and mu_i,j(x), determine whether the full PDE system is well posed and determine the asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution.
target_in_paper: The concluding open problem on Baohe Su’s 1997 supplementary-variable PDE model for a two dissimilar unit system with three modes and random check: determine whether the full time-dependent system is well posed and determine the asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the specific model targeted by the open problem: Su’s 1997 supplementary-variable system for a two dissimilar unit system with three modes and random check. It also correctly singles out the two paper-faithful objectives: (i) well-posedness of the full time-dependent PDE system, and (ii) asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution. The named state probabilities and rate functions match the official formulation of this open problem.
missing_details: The system is not finite-dimensional: p_{0,0,k}(x,t) is indexed by all k >= 0, so the problem is an infinite coupled transport system, not just the listed components.

The full transport equations must be stated explicitly, including the coupling terms sum_{k>=0} lambda_{0,1} p_{0,0,k}(x,t) and sum_{k>=0} lambda_{1,0} p_{0,0,k}(x,t), and the mixed-mode equation for p_{1,1,0}(x,t).

The boundary conditions at x=0 are essential and were omitted in the draft: p_{0,0,0}(0,t), p_{0,0,k}(0,t) for k>=1, and the boundary conditions for p_{0,1,1}, p_{1,0,1}, p_{0,2,0}, p_{2,0,0}, p_{1,1,1}, p_{1,2,0}, p_{2,1,0}, as well as the zero boundary conditions for p_{0,1,0}, p_{1,0,0}, p_{1,1,0}.
The initial data are part of the official formulation and must be included: p_{0,0,0}(x,0)=delta(x), p_{0,0,k}(x,0)=0 for k>=1, and all remaining components vanish initially.

The positivity/divergence assumptions on the rate functions are missing: alpha(x) >= 0 with integral from 0 to infinity of alpha(x) dx = infinity; similarly integral divergence conditions for each mu_{i,0}, mu_{0,i}, and mu_{i,j}.
The official notation includes the interpretation of the state probabilities; without these, the question is not fully stand-alone.
The meaning of well posed must be specified in a state space compatible with Dirac masses in the boundary and initial conditions; otherwise existence/uniqueness is ambiguous.
Because the data contain delta distributions, one must specify whether the sought solution is classical, mild, weak, or measure/distribution valued.
The asymptotic question should specify the long-time regime t -> infinity and whether the issue is convergence to a steady-state solution, and in what topology/sense.
The positivity of the constant failure rates lambda_{1,0}, lambda_{2,0}, lambda_{0,1}, lambda_{0,2} should be stated explicitly.

There is no relevant ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, or nilpotency condition in this PDE/reliability setting; the analogous missing structural data are the Banach state space, admissible solution class, and quantifiers on k and t.
refined_question: Consider Su’s 1997 supplementary-variable model for a two dissimilar unit system with three modes and random check, with state variables p_{0,0,k}(x,t) (k>=0), p_{1,0,0}(x,t), p_{0,1,0}(x,t), p_{0,1,1}(x,t), p_{1,0,1}(x,t), p_{0,2,0}(x,t), p_{2,0,0}(x,t), p_{1,1,0}(x,t), p_{1,1,1}(x,t), p_{1,2,0}(x,t), and p_{2,1,0}(x,t), governed for x,t>=0 by partial_t p_{0,0,k}+partial_x p_{0,0,k}=-(lambda_{0,1}+lambda_{1,0}+alpha(x))p_{0,0,k} (k>=0); partial_t p_{0,1,0}+partial_x p_{0,1,0}=-(lambda_{1,0}+lambda_{0,2}+alpha(x))p_{0,1,0}+sum_{k>=0} lambda_{0,1} p_{0,0,k}; partial_t p_{1,0,0}+partial_x p_{1,0,0}=-(lambda_{0,1}+lambda_{2,0}+alpha(x))p_{1,0,0}+sum_{k>=0} lambda_{1,0} p_{0,0,k}; partial_t p_{0,1,1}+partial_x p_{0,1,1}=-mu_{0,1}(x)p_{0,1,1}; partial_t p_{1,0,1}+partial_x p_{1,0,1}=-mu_{1,0}(x)p_{1,0,1}; partial_t p_{0,2,0}+partial_x p_{0,2,0}=-mu_{0,2}(x)p_{0,2,0}; partial_t p_{2,0,0}+partial_x p_{2,0,0}=-mu_{2,0}(x)p_{2,0,0}; partial_t p_{1,1,0}+partial_x p_{1,1,0}=-(lambda_{0,2}+lambda_{2,0}+alpha(x))p_{1,1,0}+lambda_{1,0}p_{0,1,0}+lambda_{0,1}p_{1,0,0}; partial_t p_{1,1,1}+partial_x p_{1,1,1}=-mu_{1,1}(x)p_{1,1,1}; partial_t p_{1,2,0}+partial_x p_{1,2,0}=-mu_{1,2}(x)p_{1,2,0}; partial_t p_{2,1,0}+partial_x p_{2,1,0}=-mu_{2,1}(x)p_{2,1,0}. Impose the boundary conditions p_{0,0,0}(0,t)=delta(t)+int_0^infinity [mu_{0,1}(x)p_{0,1,1}(x,t)+mu_{1,0}(x)p_{1,0,1}(x,t)+mu_{0,2}(x)p_{0,2,0}(x,t)+mu_{2,0}(x)p_{2,0,0}(x,t)+mu_{1,2}(x)p_{1,2,0}(x,t)+mu_{2,1}(x)p_{2,1,0}(x,t)+mu_{1,1}(x)p_{1,1,1}(x,t)] dx, p_{0,0,k}(0,t)=int_0^infinity alpha(x)p_{0,0,k-1}(x,t) dx for k>=1, p_{0,1,0}(0,t)=p_{1,0,0}(0,t)=p_{1,1,0}(0,t)=0, p_{0,1,1}(0,t)=int_0^infinity alpha(x)p_{0,1,0}(x,t) dx, p_{1,0,1}(0,t)=int_0^infinity alpha(x)p_{1,0,0}(x,t) dx, p_{0,2,0}(0,t)=int_0^infinity lambda_{0,2}p_{0,1,0}(x,t) dx, p_{2,0,0}(0,t)=int_0^infinity lambda_{2,0}p_{1,0,0}(x,t) dx, p_{1,1,1}(0,t)=int_0^infinity alpha(x)p_{1,1,0}(x,t) dx, p_{1,2,0}(0,t)=int_0^infinity lambda_{0,2}p_{1,1,0}(x,t) dx, and p_{2,1,0}(0,t)=int_0^infinity lambda_{2,0}p_{1,1,0}(x,t) dx, together with initial data p_{0,0,0}(x,0)=delta(x), p_{0,0,k}(x,0)=0 for k>=1, and all other components initially zero. Assume lambda_{1,0}, lambda_{2,0}, lambda_{0,1}, lambda_{0,2} > 0, alpha(x) >= 0 with int_0^infinity alpha(x) dx = infinity, mu_{i,0}(x) >= 0 and int_0^infinity mu_{i,0}(x) dx = infinity for i=1,2, mu_{0,i}(x) >= 0 and int_0^infinity mu_{0,i}(x) dx = infinity for i=1,2, and mu_{i,j}(x) >= 0 with int_0^infinity mu_{i,j}(x) dx = infinity for i,j in {1,2}. In a natural Banach lattice/state space compatible with the Dirac boundary and initial data, does this full infinite coupled PDE system admit a unique positive time-dependent solution depending continuously on the data, and what is the asymptotic behavior of that solution as t -> infinity, in particular whether it converges to a steady-state solution?
justification: The draft is clearly not targeting the main solved problem advertised in the abstract of arXiv:2405.11510, which concerns Li and Cao’s stochastic scheduling model on an unreliable machine; rather, it matches the notation, rates, and objective of the Su 1997 open problem previously formulated by the same author. The abstract of arXiv:2405.11510 confirms that the paper ends by leaving open problems. Among Gupur’s previously formulated open problems, the Su model is the unique one whose state labels p_{0,0,k}, p_{1,0,0}, p_{0,1,0}, p_{1,1,0}, p_{0,1,1}, p_{1,0,1}, p_{0,2,0}, p_{2,0,0}, p_{1,1,1}, p_{1,2,0}, p_{2,1,0} and rates lambda_{1,0}, lambda_{2,0}, lambda_{0,1}, lambda_{0,2}, alpha, mu_{i,0}, mu_{0,i}, mu_{i,j} exactly coincide with your draft. The nearest official formulation is therefore the statement that, after the full PDE/boundary/initial system is written down and the rate assumptions are specified, 'Well-posedness of the system of the above equations and asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution have not been obtained until now.' I therefore kept your scope exactly there and only added the missing quantifiers, boundary and initial data, solution-class issues forced by the Dirac masses, and the infinite-dimensional nature of the k-indexed family. Since the accessible web copy of the arXiv page gives only the abstract, the exact mathematical formulation has to be anchored to Gupur’s earlier explicit statement of the same open problem; I have not broadened it beyond that statement.
